description: NexaMusic 0.1.4 Beta — Radio and Explore redesign, Pod selection polish, and discovery UI improvements.

changelog.title: What's new
items: Introduced Apple Music V3 lyrics as a beta style, with improved typography, spacing, word timing, and smoother lyric auto-scrolling.
Improved duet and multi-vocalist lyric alignment so each singer's lines retain their identity and positioning.
Added animated interlude indicators and refined timed-lyrics rendering.
Refreshed Search colours and Settings icons with a more consistent, colourful Apple Music-inspired appearance.
Restored YouTube Music playlist synchronization in the Library.
Fixed guest playback truncation on streams that do not report their total length.
Improved transition timing and playback handoff behaviour.
Optimized lyrics rendering, Liquid Glass effects, and tab animations to reduce unnecessary work.
Added a sign-in reminder for logged-out users, with a preference to hide it.
Added automatic update checks, beta-release support, background APK downloads, and update notifications.
Moved the Pod BETA label out of the playback screen and into the Player Style selection, where users choose Pod.
Redesigned Radio station cards so artwork stays unobstructed, station names and first tracks sit below covers, and the on-air station has a dedicated hero card.
Made the red ON AIR hero appear only while a radio station is actively playing; it stays hidden when playback is paused, stopped, or playing unrelated content.
Redesigned Explore featured albums, release shelves, and mood tiles with clean cover-first layouts and a stable, non-repeating flat-colour palette.
Removed artwork-derived blur and tint from the Radio and Explore top chrome so titles and status-bar areas stay readable.
Added shared Smooth Header geometry and motion tokens for consistent scroll-driven header work across screens.
Removed the fixed theme-colour strip from the Radio and Explore tab-header path; both now use the shared page-colour TopFadeBlur treatment.
Reduced Search header tint from 90% to the shared 62% page-colour peak so its top chrome no longer reads as a solid band.
Centralized additional Smooth Header typography and blur-saturation tokens for the shared header contract.
Fixed Smooth Blur Header integration imports and kept the shared tab header on the progressive page-colour fade.
Applied the shared large-title fade, upward movement, and scale curve to reusable scrolling screen scaffolds, with the compact title following the same collapse progress.
Added unit coverage for shared scroll-progress, title handoff, blur opacity, and profile/title scale token boundaries.
Made the shared top blur scroll-aware and connected Search browse scrolling so its blur/tint is clear at the top and progressively appears as content moves beneath the header.
Connected History's artwork-tinted header blur and compact title to its existing scroll-collapse progress.
Added a shared scroll-progress signal so the persistent top blur follows the active destination rather than remaining visible at rest.
Connected Home, Radio, Explore, and Library vertical scrolling to the shared Smooth Blur Header progress signal.
Kept Home's existing feed-scroll tracker and attached the shared header observer without adding per-item collectors.
Connected local-only Home scrolling to the same shared header progress signal.
Connected the Settings hub, reusable Settings pages, and custom Settings scaffolds to shared header scroll progress.
Connected Changelog, Party, and Update vertical scrolling to the shared header progress signal.
Connected Album, Artist, and local/online/automatic/cache/top Playlist artwork-detail scrolling to their progressive top blur.
Added the shared ScrollHeaderScaffold and six-pass ProgressiveBlurLayer with the exact 0.5–24dp blur radii, progressive masks, 1.2 saturation, 62% theme tint, and 90dp scroll handoff.
Connected restored scroll offsets to the shared progress signal across Home, Radio, Library, Explore, Search, History, Settings, Changelog, Update, Album, Artist, Playlist, and Now Playing.
Separated Search's YouTube Music / Your Library switch into a pinnable row that locks beneath the compact title after it scrolls out of the grid.
Removed fixed header scrims and bands from Album, Artist, all Playlist detail variants, Update, and the Now Playing status-bar strip; retained artwork and existing controls.
Added API/device capability fallback, battery-saver and low-RAM scrims, reduced-transparency styling, reduced-motion crossfades, and a repeated slow-frame session fallback.
Made status and navigation bars transparent with icon contrast selected from the app's active Appearance theme.
Recorded the existing Haze 1.3.1 Apache-2.0 attribution in NOTICE; no additional blur library or dependency was introduced.
Expanded Smooth Header unit tests for all six blur radii, mask endpoints, fallback opacity, header geometry, and reduced-motion duration.

changelog.title: Notes
items: Apple Music V3 lyrics are still in beta; timing and alignment can vary by track and lyrics provider.
Playlist synchronization requires a signed-in YouTube Music account.
Playback transitions and performance should be verified across different devices and tracks.
Dark/light appearance and device-specific scrolling performance still require physical-device verification.
Automated token tests cover the shared motion math; full UI, accessibility, fallback, refresh-rate, and physical-device tests are not yet verified.
Smooth Blur Header code now uses one shared scroll-progress contract, a six-layer masked Haze stack, theme-derived tint, and a pinnable Search source row.

Fallback policy: API below 31, battery saver, low-RAM or low-performance devices use the 85% theme scrim; Reduce transparency uses 92%; Reduce motion crossfades titles over 150ms; repeated slow frames switch to scrim for the rest of the session.
Haze 1.3.1 is already present in the project and is Apache-2.0 licensed; its attribution is recorded in NOTICE.
Automated token tests cover the design constants. CI and physical-device verification are tracked separately; no 60/120fps or low-end-device measurement is claimed until run.
